text.p: Italian bond futures held to lower levels in late afternoon trading reflecting a slightly easier lira against the mark and concerns by investors over the upcoming 1997 Italian financial budget, dealers said.
"It was a pretty quiet day out there with the LIFFE December contract trading in a tight 27 basis point range throughout the day," said one LIFFE dealer.

U.S. August Producers Price Index inflation figures showed a tame U.S. inflation picture, and had little impact on prices of Italian BTPs which continued to suffer in comparison to German bunds and U.S. T-bonds.

The U.S. August PPI rose 0.3 percent with the core rate falling 0.1 percent, after an expected rise of 0.1 percent for both rates. Dealers said that market attention is now on U.S. consumer price inflation due on Friday.
Dealers said trading in BTPs was largely subdued throughout he day with some investors concerned about the budget process and some unsettled by the lira/mark exchange rate.

Fluctuations in the lira/mark rate were caused after reported remarks, subsequently strongly denied, that a Treasury undersecretary had stated that the lira would enter the ERM around a rate of 1,020 lire to the German mark.
